title: Cop-win graphs are exactly the dismantlable graphs (Nowakowski-Winkler), and trees have cop number 1
abstract: A machine-checked proof of the Nowakowski-Winkler theorem in the game of cops and robbers: a finite graph has cop number 1 if and only if it is dismantlable. A vertex u is a corner if some other vertex w has N[u] contained in N[w] (closed neighbourhoods), and a graph is dismantlable if corners can be deleted one at a time until one vertex is left. The proof defines a one-cop game played inside a vertex set, with a bridge lemma showing that on the whole vertex set it is exactly Formal Conjectures' game CopsCatchWithin with one cop. A general shadow-map lemma says that if f maps S into T, sends legal moves to legal moves, and a cop on f x can reach every vertex the robber can step to from x, then a cop that wins on T also wins on S, by chasing the robber's shadow f r. Folding a corner onto the vertex that covers it is such a map, so induction on dismantlability gives one direction. For the converse, following the robber's longest escape gives a corner just before capture: the robber's vertex, covered by the cop's. Folding that corner away is a retract, and a cop that wins on a set also wins on any retract of it by standing on the image of its position, so induction on the number of vertices shows every cop-win finite graph is dismantlable. As a corollary, every finite nonempty tree is dismantlable (each leaf is a corner covered by its neighbour) and so has cop number 1. This is the statement meyniel_conjecture.variants.tree of Formal Conjectures, which marks it research solved. The mathematics is classical and no mathematical priority is claimed; to our knowledge this is the first published Lean 4 formalisation.
